mnemonics.title: MONA
mnemonics.for: Immediate treatment for a myocardial infarction (MI)

letters.m: Morphine — relieves pain and reduces oxygen demand
Oxygen — if the client is hypoxic
Aspirin — antiplatelet, chewed for fast absorption

mnemonics.explain: Give in the order Aspirin → Oxygen → Nitroglycerin → Morphine in practice, but 'MONA' is how you remember the four.

mnemonics.title: VEAL CHOP
mnemonics.explain: Line up VEAL over CHOP: each letter maps to its cause. Late = placental = stop oxytocin, reposition, O₂.

mnemonics.title: RACE
mnemonics.for: What to do when there is a fire
mnemonics.explain: RACE is the order of actions in a fire. Pair it with PASS for using the extinguisher.

mnemonics.title: PASS
mnemonics.for: How to use a fire extinguisher

letters.m: Aim at the base of the fire

mnemonics.explain: Aim at the BASE of the flames, not the top.

mnemonics.title: FAST
mnemonics.explain: Sudden onset of any of these = call for help immediately; time is brain.

mnemonics.title: SLUDGE
mnemonics.explain: Cholinergic crisis = too much 'wet.' Antidote is atropine (dries secretions).

mnemonics.title: 6 P's
mnemonics.for: Signs of compartment syndrome / neurovascular compromise
mnemonics.explain: Pain out of proportion + paresthesia are the earliest. Pulselessness/paralysis are late — an emergency.

mnemonics.title: ADPIE
mnemonics.explain: When a question asks what to do FIRST, the answer is usually Assess.

mnemonics.title: SIG E CAPS
mnemonics.explain: Five or more for 2+ weeks suggests major depression. Always screen for the last S — suicide.

mnemonics.title: CAGE
mnemonics.for: Quick screening for alcohol use disorder

letters.m: Annoyed by others criticizing your drinking?
Eye-opener — a drink first thing in the morning?

mnemonics.explain: Two or more 'yes' answers is a positive screen warranting further assessment.

mnemonics.title: PQRST

letters.m: Region/Radiation — where and does it spread

mnemonics.explain: A structured pain history. Pain is subjective — believe the client's report.

mnemonics.title: Never Let Monkeys Eat Bananas
mnemonics.for: Order of WBC differential (most to least)
mnemonics.explain: Neutrophils are the most abundant and the first responders to bacterial infection.

mnemonics.title: On Old Olympus' Towering Tops
mnemonics.explain: For sensory/motor/both, use: 'Some Say Marry Money But My Brother Says Big Brains Matter Most.'

mnemonics.title: 5 Rights
mnemonics.explain: Some add Right documentation, reason, and response. Verify before every med.

mnemonics.title: Cushing's Triad
mnemonics.for: Late signs of increased intracranial pressure (ICP)
mnemonics.explain: The OPPOSITE of shock. It's a late, ominous sign of impending brain herniation.

mnemonics.title: C BIG K Drop

letters.m: Insulin + Glucose — shifts K⁺ into cells
Kayexalate — removes K⁺ via the gut
Dialysis/Diuretics — remove K⁺ from the body

mnemonics.explain: Calcium first to stabilize the heart, then shift potassium in, then remove it from the body.

mnemonics.title: RICE
mnemonics.for: First aid for a sprain or strain
mnemonics.explain: Ice early to reduce swelling; heat is used later for chronic stiffness.

mnemonics.title: SMART Goals
mnemonics.explain: A good outcome is client-centered and measurable: 'Client will ambulate 50 ft by day 2.'

mnemonics.title: Cold & Clammy vs Hot & Dry
mnemonics.explain: Hypoglycemia comes on fast: shaky, sweaty, confused — treat with 15 g fast carbs.

mnemonics.title: Air = MTV
mnemonics.explain: Airborne = N95 respirator + negative-pressure room. Droplet and contact are separate.

mnemonics.title: Clear Before Cloudy
mnemonics.for: Order for mixing insulins in one syringe

letters.m: Draw up the CLEAR (regular/rapid) insulin first
Then draw up the CLOUDY (NPH) insulin

mnemonics.explain: Draw clear first so you never contaminate the vial of clear insulin with cloudy. Only regular insulin is given IV.

mnemonics.title: Trousseau & Chvostek

letters.m: Carpal spasm when a BP cuff is inflated
Facial twitch when the cheek is tapped

mnemonics.explain: Both signal neuromuscular irritability from low calcium (watch after thyroidectomy).
